newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico shrs rise on Telmex, Carso to record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico shrs rise on Telmex, Carso to record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks surged to a record close for the second day in a row on Tuesday, on the back of market heavyweights and forecast primary rate falls, traders said. Analysts urged caution, however, saying that gains could be a short-lived New Year phenomenon.
"It was basically Telmex and Carso, again, although forecast rate falls at the primary auction obviously helped," a trader said.
The blue chip .MXX index closed up 23.96 points, or 0.69 percent, at 3,516.13. Volume .TV.MX was moderate at 82.1 million shares traded.
Telecommunications firm Telmex and holding company Grupo Carso closed up 32 and 40 centavos, respectively, at 14.32 and 45.80 pesos. Telmex ADRs gained 3/8 to 36-1/4 on Wall Street.
A Reuters survey of money market traders showed an average forecast rate of 24.78 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes at Tuesday evening's primary auction, or 93 basis points below last week's rate.

Analysts noted that while Mexican stocks had lagged their counterparts in New York and a rally was "overdue," Monday's and Tuesday's gains could still be mainly due to fund managers rearranging portfolios in the New Year.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.3 centavos firmer, at 7.8340/7.8380 per dollar.
On the broad market, a total of 110 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered decliners by 46 to 43.
At the head of the gainers .PG.MX, analysts noted the presence of paper firm Kimber and cement makers Apasco, up 6.30 and 1.60 pesos, respectively, at 55.70 and 161.80 pesos.
"Foreigners like Kimber and especially Apasco, as it's owned by Holderbank," Almazn said.
Traders noted retail firm Cifra was one heavily traded gainer, saying it was recovering from a poor year in 1996.
